Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Global Asset Management Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. [Operator Instructions] Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Global Asset Management's Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Investment Officer; Lisa Wong, Head of Distribution; Robert Kline, Head of Operations; Elena Vasquez, Head of Risk Management; and Jordan Lee, Head of Technology.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by our accelerated organic growth rate and expanding market share. Our organic growth rate hit 8.7% year-over-year in the quarter, up from 6.2% in the prior quarter and well ahead of the industry's blended 4.9%, according to Morningstar Direct data. This organic expansion comes from market appreciation contributing 5.2%, powered by our equity portfolios capturing 102% of the MSCI World Index's 7.8% return through tactical overweights in U.S. large-cap growth like the Magnificent Seven, alongside fixed income gains from the Fed's recent 50 basis point rate cut yielding 3.1% in core aggregate strategies versus the Bloomberg U.S. Aggregate's 2.4%. Net inflows added another layer, with $28.4 billion total and $22.1 billion in long-term flows, 92% from existing clients highlighting our sticky franchise. Separately managed accounts led with $12.6 billion, up 22% year-over-year, thanks to our TaxGuard Alpha Engine delivering 45 basis points of after-tax outperformance in equity SMAs.

By asset class, ETFs saw 12.4% organic growth, pushing AUM past $450 billion, with our flagship Apex S&P 500 ETF gathering $8.2 billion and lifting market share to 1.8% in large-cap core, making us the number four provider by flows per ETFGI, driven by our 3 basis point expense ratio and ESG screens attracting 35% sustainable inflows. Alternatives grew 9.8% organically with $6.7 billion into private credit and infrastructure, like Apex Private Credit Fund III targeting 10-12% net IRRs, oversubscribed by European pensions and boosting our global alternatives share to 2.3% per Preqin, ahead of Ares and Apollo in direct lending.

Regionally, North America at 62% of our $1.35 trillion AUM grew 9.2% organically, expanding U.S. equity share to 2.4% via wirehouse strength like $10.2 billion from Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley RIAs shifting to model-delivery portfolios. EMEA grew 6.8% despite UK gilt volatility, gaining 0.3% share to 1.9% in continental Europe through UCITS ETFs and the Euro Sustainable Equity Fund drawing €4.2 billion from Dutch and Nordic APFs under SFDR. APAC shone at 11.5% with $4.8 billion into Hong Kong-domiciled ETFs on Greater China tech, lifting active APAC equity share to 1.2% versus BlackRock's iShares per Cerulli, via our AI-powered thematic platform.

Firm-wide, U.S. market share across active and passive reached 2.1% of the $75 trillion domestic AUM per Investment Company Institute, up 10 basis points year-over-year and outpacing the Big Three in flow share at 3.2% of industry totals. Passive equities hit 1.7%, active fixed income 2.8%, and globally we're at 1.1% of $120 trillion, with upside in retirement services growing 14.2% via 401(k) wraps and our Apex Bitcoin ETP in Europe at $1.2 billion AUM. This stems from our NextGen Distribution Platform boosting retention to 96.5%, multi-asset solutions like Apex Target 2050 Fund with $3.1 billion inflows blending 60/40 and alts for DC plans, and innovations like tokenized real assets with Securitize for the $16 trillion tokenization wave per BCG. Looking forward, we see Q4 organic growth of 7-9% on Fed easing and a $50 billion institutional pipeline, hedged defensively. Our AUM grew to $2.05 trillion.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. From a financial perspective, Apex Global Asset Management delivered strong results in Q3 FY24. Our revenue was $1.45 billion, representing an 18% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by robust net flows by channel—institutional, retail, and alternatives—which totaled $18.2 billion for the quarter, our strongest since Q4 2021 and up 25% sequentially from Q2's $14.5 billion, with year-to-date at $48.7 billion above our 3-4% long-term organic AUM growth average. Excluding $3.1 billion market appreciation and $1.2 billion FX tailwinds from a stronger euro and yen, core organic flows showed resilience amid VIX at 22, U.S. inflation at 3.2%, and Fed/ECB rates at 5.25-5.50% and 4.50%, as clients shifted to derisking, income products, and inflation hedges.

Institutional led with $12.4 billion or 68% of total, up 18% quarter-over-quarter and 4.2% organic on a $1.2 trillion base—now 62% of total AUM, up from 58% a year ago for its low-beta stickiness. Drivers included $4.8 billion fixed income from Apex Core Plus Bond Fund and LDI overlays on rising 10-year Treasury to 4.8%, $3.2 billion equities in large-cap value and quality SMAs with active alpha. North America $6.8 billion from Taft-Hartley reallocations, EMEA $3.5 billion via Paris-aligned ESG for Dutch/UK schemes despite UCITS outflows, APAC $2.1 billion from GIC/Temasek in infrastructure debt. Initiatives like API integrations with Envestnet/SEI drove 30% inflows, plus two $1.5 billion OCIO mandates and PBGC premium tailwinds.

Retail delivered $4.1 billion or 23%, rebounding from Q2's $1.8 billion at 2.8% organic on $450 billion base—28% of total AUM. $2.7 billion into ETFs like Apex US Dividend Aristocrats ETF (DIVA) at $900 million and $2.5 billion AUM since May launch, $1.0 billion active mutuals in target-dates, $400 million RIA SMAs. U.S. 72% or $3.0 billion via Morgan Stanley/Merrill no-loads post-DOL rules, Europe $700 million flat on PRIIPs but gaining via UCITS ETFs, Asia $400 million on MPF. Apex Direct robo-advisor onboarded 150,000 accounts with BlackRock Aladdin tech at 25 bps wraps, plus fractional shares for millennial HNWIs; fees at 42 bps down 50 bps but ETF scale at 15% offsets.

Alternatives hit a record $1.7 billion or 9%, 35% YoY growth on $250 billion base—12% of total. Private credit $900 million including $500 million Apex Direct Lending Fund V (12-14% IRR) with CalPERS-like anchor, real assets $500 million in infrastructure equity via IIEF for data centers/renewables, hedge $300 million multi-strat for family offices. North America 45% or $770 million from endowments/FoFs, EMEA $500 million Middle East SWFs, APAC $430 million Japan GPIF pilots. Scaling evergreen with $1 billion private credit interval and $750 million real estate ETF-likes in Q4, GP stakes like 20% in PE boutique; fees at 95 bps with 200 bps carry upside. Diversified flows grew AUM to $2.05 trillion, +7% QoQ; Q4 flows $15-20 billion on $10 billion pipeline, 60% institutional, resilient with 45% active/passive and 35% ESG.

Our expenses were $750 million, resulting in net income of $450 million. Our expense ratio improved due to operating leverage. Our operating expenses totaled $428 million for the quarter, up 4.2% year-over-year but down 1.8% sequentially, with year-to-date at $1.27 billion up 5.1%. Supporting $1.2 trillion AUM with $28 billion inflows into passive ETFs like our $150 billion Apex S&P 500 ETF on AI rally, amid fee compression to 32 bps from 33 bps, expense ratio fell to 52 bps of average AUM from 55 bps.

Compensation and benefits at $256 million or 60%, up 6.3% on 3.2% headcount to 4,200 focused on PMs/client roles for 15% alts growth; variable up 12% on 18% organic but moderated. APAC up 22% hiring 45 for Apex Asia ex-Japan Equity on Nikkei highs, EMEA flat via Dublin hub. Total Rewards 2.0 with ESG-linked comp like BlackRock.

Technology and data $68 million or 16%, up 12.4% on $25 million AWS/ApexOne cloud—processing 2 petabytes daily; gen-AI cut research 30%, ESG feeds for $300 billion sustainable up 25% on SFDR. U.S. 65% for Apex Digital Wealth at $50 billion, LATAM blockchain for crypto post-Bitcoin ETFs.

Distribution/marketing $52 million or 12%, up 2.1% with 15% better cost per inflow; ETF campaigns, Wealthfront SMAs, APAC roadshows for $10 billion SWFs, EMEA down 5% on PRIIPs.

G&A $38 million or 9% flat, audit/legal for boutique fixed income tuck-in, occupancy down 7%. Amort/deprec $14 million or 3% down 5.6%. Q4 OpEx $440-450 million, full-year 4-5% growth below 6% guide on $20 million savings; levers like 45% ETF AUM at 15 bps, ApexOne AI 10-15% savings, EMEA hubs. Targeting 28-30% margins FY25 ahead of State Street.

Compensation ratio was 48.2% for the quarter and 47.2% full-year, up slightly from 46.8% and 45.5% but in 45-50% target, competitive to BlackRock's 46% and T. Rowe's 49%. On $4.8 billion FY revenue up 9% from $45 billion ETF/alts inflows, comp up 13% to $2.27 billion. Fixed 22% flat on headcount discipline—150 quants/data scientists for Pinnacle Alpha Engine, 80 RMs. Variable 25.2% from $320 million perf fees up 25%, deferred equity on TSR.

Americas 49.5% on talent wars vs. Renaissance/Citadel, 15% RSU boosts for PMs. EMEA 46.8% post-Brexit, APAC 43.2% down 100 bps via Singapore/Tokyo for Asia ex-Japan up 18%. Investments: $150 million AI upskilling cut small-cap headcount 5%, clawbacks on 40% incentives. 2024 guide 46-48% on AUM growth; levers Alpha Engine 10-15% efficiencies, alts to 25%, Mumbai insights, ESG comp 20% on net-zero.

On M&A, we closed $1.4 billion EuroGreen Partners acquisition—Paris boutique $10.2 billion AUM in SFDR Article 9 sustainable infra/real assets—for 14x fees, accretive 8% FY24 to 15% FY26 on $65 million synergies migrating to our Aladdin system, cutting OpEx 25%; 98% retention, cross-sell to $450 billion institutional for ESG now $320 billion up 22%. Announced $2.1 billion APEP—Singapore $14.5 billion ASEAN tech/ETFs—at 16x, Q1 FY25 close adding to $120 billion Asia ex-Japan doubled in three years for $1.2 trillion TAM. Synergies $80 million costs, $150 million revenue via AI NLP integration. Pipeline $50-75 billion: 40% alts secondaries, 30% digital wealth, 30% EM fixed. Up 25% industry volumes to $120 billion per PwC on scale needs.

AUM ended Q3 at $892 billion up 8% quarter-over-quarter, 14% year-over-year—11th straight positive organic quarter. Flows $18.2 billion Q3, YTD $52.4 billion outperforming industry's $1.1 trillion per Morningstar. ETFs $12.5 billion led by PINQ $4.2 billion on S&P rally, active PING $3.1 billion; fixed $4.8 billion core bonds; alts $2.3 billion Direct Lending at $8.5 billion. Outflows $1.4 billion legacy active equities to UCITS/ETFs. Institutional $9.7 billion, retail/RIA $8.5 billion via Aladdin platform for 4,200 RIAs. North America $13.8 billion 76%, EMEA $2.9 billion ESG ETFs +150 bps share vs. iShares, APAC $1.5 billion Hong Kong ETFs. Markets +$14.7 billion, fees 32 bps.

Q4 flows $15-20 billion, FY24 $67-72 billion up 28-32%; AUM $940-960 billion end-24, 12-15% organic. FY25 $80-100 billion inflows, AUM $1.05-1.10 trillion. Drivers: Q1 2025 ETFs—buffered equity, private real assets $5 billion Year 1, AI/ML SMA; PinnacleOne gen-AI by mid-2025 +30% SMA; APAC headcount to 120 with Yu'e Bao, EMEA AIFMD privates €10 billion. Tailwinds: $84 trillion wealth transfer, $25 trillion DC/IM, alts to 18%. Hedged 60% beta-neutral, 8% cash.

David Patel: Thank you, Michael. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities. We are navigating the current market environment by realizing $285 million in performance fees in Q2, up 32% quarter-over-quarter and 18% year-over-year, YTD $812 million strongest since 2021—25% of trailing fee income on high-water marks, 8% hurdle, quarterly crystallization where applicable. From $142 billion fee-eligible AUM up 11% on inflows and outperformance.

Equities 42% generated $186 million; Global Equity Fund $28 billion AUM 6.2% Q2 vs. S&P 500 5.1% +110 bps, YTD +320 bps at 18.4% vs. 15.1% on NVIDIA/Microsoft AI, cyclicals underweight staples. U.S. Large-Cap Growth +1.8% 1-year via AlphaForge ML satellite data; Euro Equity 4.9% vs. STOXX 600 +90 bps on ECB cuts, Novo Nordisk; EM Alpha 3.2% vs. MSCI EM 2.8% Q2 but -150 bps YTD trimmed China to 12% into India tech. Sharpe 1.42 vs. S&P 1.12, drawdown -4.2%.

Fixed/credit 28% $52 million up 45%; Core Bond $19 billion 2.1% vs. Agg 0.9% +120 bps, YTD +190 bps at 4.3% vs. 2.4% on duration 6.2 years, IG corporates 5.3%. High Yield 7.8% vs. ICE HY 6.4% +140 bps YTD +310 bps on BB energy/loans spreads 420 to 380 bps; EM Debt 4.5% vs. JPM EMBI 4.2% 1-year +2.1% Argentina/Brazil.

Alts/multi 30% $47 million; Absolute Return $14 billion 5.6% vs. HFRI 3.9% +170 bps YTD +12.8% vs. 7.2% on semis/private credit 11% IRR; Climate Alpha $2.5 billion 8.1% vs. MSCI ESG +2.3%. 85% above high-water, 62% crystallized; countering 45 to 52 bps fee drop with 20/2 alts feeders AI Quant Equity $1B, Private Credit $3B on $50 million ML R&D. 1/3/5-year medians +1.6/+2.1/+1.8% vs. benchmarks vs. BlackRock/PIMCO. Election/China mitigants: Monte Carlo, 60/40 tools.

We launched Apex AI Quant Equity Fund this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $1 billion in seed inflows and outperformance via ML predictive alpha.

Lisa Wong: Thank you, David. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in APAC are paying off, as evidenced by the key drivers behind these net flows—superior fund performance, market trends, and strategic initiatives. Net client flows totaled $12.5 billion in the quarter and $48.2 billion full-year, 6.2% QoQ and 12.8% YoY organic to record $892 billion AUM up 22%. Performance led: U.S. Large Cap Growth 28.4% vs. S&P 500 +420 bps on NVIDIA/Microsoft AI drawing $4.8 billion retail 401(k)/IRAs; Core Bond 7.2% top decile Agg + yield extension pre-Fed cuts $3.2 billion pensions; Global Real Assets 12% yield $2.1 billion inflation hedges.

Sharpe 1.45 vs. industry 1.12, 68% AUM 3-year outperformers up from 52%. Trends: S&P 24% 'Magnificent Seven' to GAPAI ETF $1.9 billion AUM $5.2 billion; SMID $1.4 billion Russell rebound; fixed $6.5 billion from money markets; ESG $7.2 billion 18% AUM $160 billion EU SFDR/U.S. SEC, Climate Transition Bond $40% retail Vanguard/Schwab. North America 62% $29.8 billion wirehouses $8.4 billion HNWI transfer; EMEA 21% $10.1 billion UK DB £500 million mandates, UCITS; APAC 15% $7.3 billion up 45% GIC/Temasek Asia ex-Japan $2.2 billion China/India.

Initiatives: five Q3 ETFs $3.1 billion incl. Semiconductor; WealthForge robo 250,000 users $1.8 billion AI personalization +22% efficiency; $4.5 billion OCIO public pension. 2024 flows $50-60 billion Fed easing/election active, $10 billion alts GP Stakes; 25% non-U.S. ballast vs. tariffs/EM.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Lisa. Operationally, we've made significant progress in streamlining our middle and back office functions. This has resulted in increased efficiency and reduced operational risk. We are also focused on maintaining tight control over operating expenses across categories. As detailed, total OpEx $428 million up 4.2% YoY but down 1.8% sequentially on $1.2 trillion AUM support, expense ratio 52 bps improved. Comp $256 million 60% up 6.3% headcount for alts; tech $68 million 16% AI/ESG; distribution $52 million 12% scale; G&A $38 million 9% flat; amort $14 million 3% down. Q4 $440-450 million, FY 4-5% growth, leverage from ETFs 45%, tech ROI, regional.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Robert. From a risk management perspective, we continue to maintain a robust framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across the organization. We have enhanced our monitoring of market volatility and are taking steps to address potential vulnerabilities. This includes close attention to our compensation ratio dynamics. At 48.2% quarterly and 47.2% full-year within 45-50% target, reflecting talent investments amid $1.2 trillion AUM up 12% on $45 billion inflows, revenue $4.8 billion +9%, comp $2.27 billion +13%. Fixed 22% steady, variable 25.2% on perf fees/deferred. Regional: Americas 49.5% competition, EMEA 46.8%, APAC 43.2%. Aligning via AI $150 million, clawbacks 40%, 2024 46-48% guide with Alpha Engine efficiencies, alts expansion, regional arbitrage, ESG-linked 20%.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Elena. On the technology front, we are investing in advanced analytics and AI to enhance our investment decision-making process and improve client service. We are also focused on strengthening our cybersecurity posture. Specifically, we've advanced ApexOne platform processing 2 petabytes daily, gen-AI research cuts 30%, ESG integrations for $300 billion AUM, cloud migrations, robo inflows, blockchain custody—tying into broader efficiencies and M&A integrations like EuroGreen/APEP AI models.

Sarah Thompson: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes our forward AUM and flow guidance: Q4 $15-20 billion flows, FY24 $67-72 billion, AUM $940-960 billion; FY25 $80-100 billion to $1.05-1.10 trillion on product launches, digital wrappers, regional pushes amid wealth transfer, DC growth, alts rise—hedged against inflation/geopolitics.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the drivers behind your strong net flows?

Sarah Thompson: Thanks, John. As Lisa highlighted, it's a mix of fund performance like our equity outperformance, market trends favoring AI/ESG, and initiatives like new ETFs and robo scaling—delivering diversified $48.2 billion full-year.

John Smith: Thank you. And a follow-up on your expense management?

Michael Chen: John, disciplined across categories with tech investments yielding leverage, comp aligned to outcomes, targeting sub-50 bps ratios long-term.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of Apex Core Bond Fund?

David Patel: Emily, the Core Bond returned 2.1% Q2 beating Agg by 120 bps, YTD +190 bps on tactical duration and IG corporates—strong risk-adjusted in hawkish pivot.

Emily Chen: And how is the new product Apex AI Quant Equity Fund performing relative to expectations?

Lisa Wong: Early inflows $1 billion exceeding targets, leveraging ML for alpha in semis/renewables, on track with APAC traction.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan.

David Lee: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Robert Kline: David, streamlining middle/back office via ApexOne digitization reduced research time 30%, automated reporting saved 10%, headcount discipline amid 15% AUM growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Gonzalez with Barclays.

Maria Gonzalez: What are your thoughts on the current regulatory environment and its impact on your risk profile?

Elena Vasquez: Maria, robust framework enhanced for SFDR/MiFID, clawbacks/ESG comp align risks; M&A like EuroGreen bolsters compliance, diversified book mitigates.

Operator: Our next question comes from Kevin Patel with BlackRock.

Kevin Patel: How are you leveraging technology to improve investment performance?

Jordan Lee: Kevin, gen-AI in AlphaForge/NLP for predictive signals, ApexOne Monte Carlo scenarios, integrating APEP models—driving Sharpe above peers.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Global Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
